searchText: Allowing the network to degrade (even slightly) and forcing another hard fork… just to keep pressure on development? <@552133098075193354> <@489256758989029405> Are we agreed that the goal is to have the block time in mid August be the same as it is today (about 14.5 seconds)? <@552133098075193354>Sir, you have been working hard recently, may I ask that Sepolia can only be obtained through mining, and there is a better way, because I don't have a good GPU Bombsten Every time the difficulty bomb gets delayed the PoW miners will gladly accept it. When the time comes that the TTD has to be set it may help if this gets packaged together with another difficulty bomb delay (Positive change+Negative change for the miners). Therefore it may be better to delay less now, and split it up into two smaller delays (The second hardfork including the TTD). Interestingly the merge fork itself doesn't have to be installed by the miners at all. It's enough if everyone else does Yes but many PoW will simply fail to switch off their miners because they wont have a very good alternative chain to switch to. If there are no good options many of them will choose to do nothing and just see what happens. If they already accepted the TTD hardfork and are already running that software it will make the chance of the PoW chain surviving much smaller. If the TTD hardfork is not packaged with any benefit to the miners most of them will just ignore it and when TTD happens the PoW chain will survive with a significant amount of mining power, a bit like the ETH and ETC split. When faced with only bad options most people will choose to simply do nothing, which in this case means keeping the miners turned on and mining the PoW chain That's why the difficulty bomb exists (and why not delaying it would be better, but too late) What I mean is, that if for example 3 months delay is needed, then it may be better to delay 2 months first, and then another 1 month packaged together with the TTD. Since the TTD is basically like a poison pill for the PoW miners it may be better to package it together with some benefit for them like another 1-2 month of mining. There is currently no coordinated effort to keep the PoW chain alive, but it could be kept alive anyway due to the tendency of people to default to doing nothing when faced with only bad options. You obviously don’t keep up with pow. When a 6700xt can make more mining rvn than eth now. Who is going to stay mining eth in a month when it’s even worse? He’s not wrong tho, ETH is 95% of GPU mining I get that but people are already starting to swap away from eth ...ravencoin has lower daily trading volume than the value of daily eth block reward what comprises that 5%? All other coins thanks. I thought etc moved to sha3 but apparently the idea was shelved 3.3% is still more than I expected Guys can I suggest to take this to #minerhugs on ethstaker discord. This is kinda cluttering a channel that core devs use to coordinate things After deliberating in the <#984847529093005312> thread, we've reached consensus: the bomb fork will be called Gray Glacier, which is a glacier who literally merges into another one 😄 It's also in the Southern Hemisphere, which we tend to neglect when picking names. Shoutout to <@403707149043105803> for the suggestion! the ECIP for Sha-3 on ETC didn't follow there current ECIP guidelines so it has to be re-introduced as a new updated ECIP if they want to bring it forward again.

Every time the difficulty bomb gets delayed the PoW miners will gladly accept it.
When the time comes that the TTD has to be set it may help if this gets packaged together with another difficulty bomb delay (Positive change+Negative change for the miners).
Therefore it may be better to delay less now, and split it up into two smaller delays (The second hardfork including the TTD).
